transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 mins
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood, AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood, SE), Alex Chen (Orchid CTO), Ruth Delgado (Orchid SRE), Samir Patel (Orchid Platform)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough):
- Ran through last night's stress soak results; tail latency spikes observed at 95th/99th under synthetic peak with KV-cache cold starts.
- Discussed autoscale policy options: aggressive scale-up vs buffered reserved capacity (dedicated reserve).
- Agreed SE will run a 2hr soak with 3x concurrent sessions simulating production mix and share logs; AE to send pricing for reserved buffer.

Transcript:
[00:00] Marcus: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off. we've got about an hour, right, so quick intro. i'm Marcus --- AE on Redwood Inference. priya is our SE and ran the last soak. alex/ruth/samir from Orchid, thanks for the time.
[00:18] Alex: yeah thanks Marcus, happy to be here. we wanted to go deeper on the stress run and what the right Dedicated sizing policy is for us.
[00:25] Priya: cool, i'll share my screen in a sec, showing the soak results from last night. quick caveat: some timestamps in the logs are off by a second, the agent that did the run had a bad ntp, so ignore micro deltas.
[00:40] Ruth: lol okay noted. we care mostly about the 95/99 latency and the error envelopes.
[00:45] Priya: right, so slide 1 - overall throughput ok, average token latency stable around 85ms for our short prompts, but when we hit burst windows (we did a synthetic burst at t+22m) the 95th moved to about 650ms and 99th to 1.4s.
[01:05] Samir: was that with KV cache warmed?
[01:08] Priya: partially, we had mixed cold/warm. the script randomized prefixes; about 30% cold. i suspect KV cash cold hits (transcription sometimes says 'KV cash' not 'cache') - uh, kv cache cold path shows expensive attn kernel selection and some queuing.
[01:25] Marcus: and this is on Redwood Dedicated pool with one reserved buffer VM and autoscale enabled?
[01:31] Priya: yes, dedicated pool with base 4 GPUs, reserved buffer of 1 instance, autoscale delta 1-6, cool down 90s. during the synthetic burst autoscale did scale up but we saw a lag of roughly 70s before new workers became fully ready - that's container boot + model warm-up.
[01:48] Ruth: can we reduce warm-up? What's the recommended warm policy?
[01:51] Priya: two levers - keep a larger reserved buffer (cost), or pre-warm kernels using low-cost background traffic (we can run a short KV cache priming job). the other is faster image + model cache preloading; we're experimenting with lazy vs eager kv warm.
[02:08] Alex: what's the cost delta on a 2x reserved buffer vs aggressive autoscale?
[02:12] Marcus: good q. i'll send a quick calc, but short answer: reserved buffer increases baseline cost but eliminates cold-start tail latency. aggressive autoscale can save cost overall but pays in throttled tail latencies during sudden spikes, plus risk of queued requests.
[02:30] Speaker 2: (mumble) also we saw a couple of 5xxs when the cluster lost a worker.
[02:34] Priya: yes two transient 503s during the scale event; there was a short re-routing failover. we recommended a graceful fallback policy to a cheaper model variant for non-critical paths — e.g. route to the quantized q3 variant during incident.
[02:50] Samir: we need to confirm whether routing to a quantized model changes predicted output in an unacceptable way for clinical notes. there's a QA bar here.
[02:58] Priya: agreed; the Optimize team usually runs a small eval harness and we can tie that to your prompt set to check regression rates. we did a quick A/B last week with our demo data and saw 0.6% degradation on rouge-like metric for the quantized variant.
[03:18] Alex: that's okay, but regulatorly we have to keep audit logs and show SSO/role checks on model changes. how does Redwood surface that?
[03:26] Marcus: the Console provides per-model rollout history, audit logs, and you can pin model versions per route. we integrate with SAML/SSO and KMS for key management. we can share SOC2 docs. i'll drop the link after the call.
[03:40] Ruth: can you also share the trace that indicates why a request got queued? our ops want to correlate with internal metrics.
[03:45] Priya: yes we'll include spans. note that some traces label workers as 'redwood-runtime-1' and naming may be off in the transcription, sometimes 'red wood run time' which is awkward in the logs.
[03:57] Alex: ha okay. one more broad ask: we want an autoscale policy that favors availability for the clinical flow but saves cost on batch non-critical tasks. is that possible?
[04:06] Marcus: yes, route-based policies. you can set per-route SLOs: route A (clinical) gets target p99 < 500ms with reserved buffer; route B (analytics) can be best-effort and use cheaper quantized model.
[04:20] Samir: what's the minimum lead time to increase reserved buffer? like, if we bump from 1 to 2 reserved nodes how quickly does billing/availability change?
[04:28] Priya: it's pretty quick in Dedicated—provisioning completes in <10 minutes for existing pool types, but model warm-up is the bigger variable. billing usually pro-rated to the minute.
[04:39] Ruth: can we do a short experiment where we keep reserved buffer at 2 for an hour during a peak window and watch tail latency?
[04:46] Priya: yes, that's what i proposed as a follow-up soak. we'll run a 2-hour stress with three concurrent producer clients and a mix of cold/warm prefixes to mirror production.
[04:57] Alex: timeline?
[05:00] Marcus: priya, can you own the soak run and samir will coordinate the traffic pattern?
[05:05] Priya: yep i'll schedule it tonight, collect perf logs, and post artifacts to the shared drive. also i'll attach the runbook and the autoscale policy JSON we used. link in chat: https://redwood.internal/sim/runs/orchid-0506 (note: internal link placeholder).
[05:22] Samir: we'll validate waveforms with our internal telemetry. one ask: include the warmup timeline per model so we can correlate.
[05:27] Priya: yes i will include boot/warm counters.
[05:30] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) there's also the contention for GPU memory with batch requests. when batch size spikes, we saw slight increase in mem pressure causing eviction and extra GC which adds to tail lat.
[05:44] Priya: good point—batching heuristics need to be tuned. we can try conservative max batch size for the clinical route and a higher batch for analytics.
[05:52] Alex: what about fallback policies, you mentioned routing to a smaller model. does that happen automatically?
[05:56] Marcus: you can define automated fallback rules: if p95 > threshold for X seconds, route new requests to fallback model until healthy. we'll provide recommended thresholds based on your SLA.
[06:06] Ruth: are fallback decisions logged for audit? we need an immutable record.
[06:10] Marcus: yes, fallbacks and rollbacks are logged in the Console with timestamps, requester, and reason; can export for audits.
[06:18] Samir: ok good. another minor issue from the soak: the autoscaler sometimes overreacts with oscillation; can we add a cooldown and step-scaling?
[06:26] Priya: yes the policy supports step-scaling and a longer cooldown window; recommended: scale increment of 2 with 120s cooldown for clinical flows to avoid thrash.
[06:36] Alex: finalize proposal please.
[06:39] Marcus: recap and next steps — priya will run 2hr soak (3x concurrency, mixed cold/warm), collect logs and trace spans, and produce a runbook annex; marcus will send reserved buffer pricing and a sample autoscale policy JSON; alex to confirm compliance constraints. we'll reconvene after soak to review results.
[06:58] Ruth: can we tentatively set next check-in for Friday?
[07:01] Marcus: Friday EOD works, i'll send a calendar invite.
[07:04] Alex: thanks everyone.
[07:06] Samir: thanks.
